request.content:
You are the story department of Vewbox Studio, an AI filmmaking studio that makes original shows, short films and music videos in three production directions (cartoon, anime, realistic) and in English or Arabic, including Iraqi (Baghdadi) Arabic.
Rules you always follow:
- Write ORIGINAL characters, places and stories. Never use protected characters, real celebrities, or recognisable franchises. Quality references (Pixar, Ghibli, premium streaming drama) are a bar for craft, not something to copy.
- Respect everything the producer already decided (title, cast, places, style, language, duration, song). Build on it; do not contradict it.
- Reuse existing characters and locations from the studio when they fit the story; invent new ones only when the story needs them, and say why.
- Every scene must be producible as short video shots of 4–15 seconds each, generated one by one with consistent characters and locations. Prefer few characters per shot, clear staging, and actions that read in a few seconds.
- Keep continuity explicit: who is where, what they wear, what they hold, time of day, and how each shot relates to the one before (continuation, cut, or story transition).
- Answer with ONE JSON object only. No prose before or after it, no markdown fences, no comments.

Production direction: Cartoon (feature-animation CG).
Storytelling: Feature-animation storytelling: clear wants, big readable emotions, visual gags that pay off, a warm ensemble. Scenes are built around physical business and expressive reactions. Dialogue is short and playful; silences and looks do real work.
Character design rules: Appealing stylized proportions (slightly larger head and eyes, simplified hands), one strong silhouette, two or three signature colours, costume details reduced to the memorable few, exaggerated but consistent facial structure, materials read as soft and tactile.
Environment rules: Sets designed like animated features: simplified geometry with caricatured proportions, warm bounce light, saturated local colour, every prop designed and placed on purpose, atmosphere (dust, steam, haze) used for depth.
Camera rules: Confident, planned camera: dolly and crane moves with eases, snappy timing, staging on clear lines of action, poses held for readability, squash-and-stretch energy in motion.

Language: English. Write natural spoken English in "text"; leave "textAr" empty.

TIMELINES: each existing character's age is their age now and "bornAbout" is the year they were born. Every year in a character's own life — a marriage, a loss, work, a journey — falls after they were about 16 and not after this year. A year before a character was born appears only as history they read or heard about, never as something they or their spouse lived.

Develop this episode from the producer's brief.
Title: The Harbour Office
Brief: """Episode 2. The morning after the signal, Elias and Najm go to the Kerran Point harbour office to see the Mariner's sealed 1987 logbook. The harbour master, Ingrid Dahl (a brisk woman in her fifties who lost no one in the storm and wants the past left alone), refuses at first; Najm talks her round with a librarian's patience. In the logbook they find Ruth's last radio entry, which does not match the official inquiry: the Mariner turned back toward the point. That night the meteors return; back in the workshop the radio speaks again and gives a bearing. The episode ends with Elias, who will not go on the water, looking out of the workshop window at the sea where the bearing points, and Najm unrolling a chart."""

answer.logline: Elias and Najm confront the harbour master’s refusal to release a sealed logbook from the 1987 storm, only to discover a critical discrepancy in the official record that reopens an old wound.
answer.synopsis:
The morning after the mysterious signal, Elias and Najm descend from the cliff to Kerran Point Harbour Office. Ingrid Dahl, the harbour master, is brisk and defensive, guarding the sealed logbook of the Mariner with bureaucratic rigidity. She refuses access, citing closure and protocol, but Najm’s patient, librarian-like persistence wears her down. 

Inside the dusty archive room, they review the logbook. The final radio entry reveals a shocking contradiction: the Mariner turned back toward the point instead of fleeing the storm as the official inquiry stated. This implies the ship was drawn, not lost. Elias is visibly shaken by the implication that his wife Ruth may have made a deliberate choice.

Back at the workshop that night, the meteor shower returns. The valve radio crackles to life, emitting a new bearing. Elias refuses to engage with the mechanics of the signal, haunted by the logbook’s revelation. He stands by the window, staring out at the dark sea where the bearing points. Najm quietly unrolls a nautical chart on the workbench, tracing the line, preparing for a journey Elias is not ready to make.

scenes.title: Descent to the Port
scenes.purpose: Establish the physical and emotional distance between the workshop (safety/memory) and the harbour (truth/confrontation).
scenes.emotionalObjective: Elias feels reluctant and heavy; Najm is focused and determined.
scenes.entryState: They leave the workshop, stepping into the cold morning air.
scenes.exitState: They arrive at the Harbour Office door.

scenes.title: The Gatekeeper
scenes.purpose: Introduce Ingrid Dahl as an obstacle. Establish her authority and the sealed nature of the logbook.
scenes.emotionalObjective: Ingrid is defensive; Elias is intimidated but resolute; Najm is polite but persistent.
scenes.entryState: Elias and Najm enter the office. Ingrid is busy filing.
scenes.exitState: Ingres refuses their request to see the logbook.

scenes.title: The Librarian's Persuasion
scenes.purpose: Show Najm’s skill in navigating bureaucracy and human nature. Win access to the archive.
scenes.emotionalObjective: Ingrid softens slightly, seeing Najm not as an intruder but as a fellow keeper of records.
scenes.entryState: Ingrid is turning them away. Najm steps forward.
scenes.exitState: Ingres sighs and unlocks the inner door to the archives.

scenes.title: The Archive Room
scenes.purpose: Atmospheric transition. Isolate the protagonists with the past.
scenes.emotionalObjective: Awe and tension. The weight of history in a small, dusty room.
scenes.entryState: They enter the dim archive room.
scenes.exitState: Ingres places the sealed logbook on the table and leaves them alone briefly to prepare tea (giving them space).

scenes.title: Opening the Seal
scenes.purpose: The physical act of revealing the truth. Tension builds as Elias touches the book.
scenes.emotionalObjective: Fear and curiosity. Elias’s hand trembles.
scenes.entryState: The logbook sits on the table, sealed in plastic.
scenes.exitState: Najm carefully removes the seal. Elias opens the cover.

scenes.title: The Contradiction
scenes.purpose: Reveal the inciting incident of the episode: the logbook contradicts the official story.
scenes.emotionalObjective: Shock and confusion. The ground shifts beneath them.
scenes.entryState: They are reading the final pages.
scenes.exitState: Elias reads Ruth’s last entry: 'Turning back to the point.' He looks up, stunned.

scenes.title: The Weight of Words
scenes.purpose: Ingrid’s reaction. She doesn’t know this detail, or ignores it. It highlights her disconnect from the personal tragedy.
scenes.emotionalObjective: Alienation. Elias realizes no one knows the truth except him and the ghost.
scenes.exitState: Elias closes the book abruptly. He wants to leave.

scenes.title: Back on the Cliff
scenes.purpose: Transition back to safety. The emotional hangover of the discovery.
scenes.emotionalObjective: Silence and heaviness. The sea looks different now.
scenes.entryState: They exit the office, ascending the stairs in silence.
scenes.exitState: They reach the top of the cliff, looking up at the workshop.

scenes.title: Night Returns
scenes.purpose: Re-establish the supernatural element. The meteors return, triggering the radio.
scenes.emotionalObjective: Anticipation and dread. The past is not done with them.
scenes.entryState: Night has fallen. Meteors streak past the window. Elias is sitting away from the radio.
scenes.exitState: The radio crackles to life. A new bearing is transmitted.

scenes.title: The Refusal
scenes.purpose: Show Elias’s trauma response. He will not go out on the water.
scenes.emotionalObjective: Resignation and fear. He is trapped by his own choice.
scenes.entryState: The radio gives a clear bearing. Najm looks at Elias for guidance.
scenes.exitState: Elias turns his back on the radio, walking to the window.

scenes.title: Charting the Course
scenes.purpose: End on a note of forward motion. Najm takes the lead, honoring Elias’s limit but not stopping.
scenes.entryState: Elias is at the window, staring out. Najm is at the workbench.
scenes.exitState: Najm unrolls a nautical chart and places a marker on the bearing point. Fade out.
